The responsibility for offering and delivering vaccinations rests with the NHS. ASC providers contribute by facilitating access, sharing relevant information and helping people to receive or attend for vaccination as needed. For instance, domiciliary and care home providers can support with booking appointments, setting up reminders, planning transport, recording vaccination status on care plans and escalating any issues or specific information required to the GP or practice nurse as required.

Vaccine status should be reviewed regularly as part of proactive care planning, for instance when onboarding, during annual reviews, after hospital discharge or following significant health changes.

The NHS vaccinations website summarises what vaccines are available for adults, and which groups of people would benefit from having them.

Always check the NHS vaccinations website, the complete routine immunisation schedule, flu vaccination for social care workers and annual flu programme as vaccinations have different age eligibility parameters and these resources will have the most up-to-date information on eligibility.

Vaccinations for care and support workers

Vaccinations for care and support workers are strongly recommended because they:

reduce the spread of preventable diseases

protect the people accessing care and support (safeguarding vulnerable adults)

reduce the severity of disease if infected

provide protection for care and support workers’ family and loved ones

keep care and support workers healthy, preventing staff shortages, service disruption, and sick leave.

reduce hospital admissions and can prevent deaths

All care and support workers are encouraged to be up to date with routine vaccination in line with the wider population. In the UK, these include for instance, tetanus, diphtheria, polio and MMR which can be accessed at any age through their GP practice. It is not too late to get these vaccines if they have been missed before.

It is the responsibility of the employer to offer access to any vaccines that are required to reduce staff members’ work-related vaccine preventable infections risks. The UK national vaccination schedule and incomplete immunisation guidance can be used by health care professionals to provide further information for non-UK born ASC staff who may have incomplete immunisation status and who may require additional vaccines to bring their status in line with the UK immunisation schedule. General recommendations on vaccines for health and care workers can be found in chapter 12 of the Green Book.

Where a care provider is not able to offer flu vaccination these can be accessed via GP or pharmacy by showing evidence of employment as a care and support worker.

Vaccination in the UK is not mandatory but is instead an individual decision based on the principle of informed consent. Documentation of care and support staff vaccination status is recommended but again is not mandatory. A record of staff vaccinations can be helpful during an outbreak of a vaccine-preventable infection, as it helps UKHSA Health Protection Teams assess the risk to staff and those they are caring for more promptly and therefore supports more effective outbreak management.

Actions for care and support workers

Care and support workers can support vaccination uptake by:

participating in annual campaigns (UKHSA/NHS) and staying up to date with their own vaccinations to help protect themselves, the people accessing care and support and their own families and loved ones

promoting uptake within their care setting

sharing up-to-date NHS information about vaccines to encourage care and support workers and the people they are caring for to take up vaccine offers when they are eligible which then helps protect everyone in the setting

encouraging people accessing care and support and their families to access vaccination services - as a member of care staff their advice is trusted and listened to

Before international travel (including visiting family and friends in a home country), check official travel advice, with enough advance, the guidance for recommended vaccinations and ensure these are obtained prior to departure. Travel vaccinations may be available through GP services, travel clinics, pharmacies or other local providers. Check local arrangements and NHS travel vaccination guidance.
